arxiv-2107-13515.title: Hopf-Galois module structure of quartic Galois extensions of ℚ \mathbb{Q}
arxiv-2107-13515.creator: Daniel Gil-Muñoz, Anna Rio
arxiv-2107-13515.description: Abstract Given a quartic Galois extension L / ℚ L/\mathbb{Q} of number fields and a Hopf-Galois structure H H on L / ℚ L/\mathbb{Q} , we study the freeness of the ring of integers 𝒪 L \mathcal{O}_{L} as module over the associated order 𝔄 H \mathfrak{A}_{H} in H H .

arxiv-2210-14711.title: Weighted pressure matching based on kernel interpolation for sound field reproduction
arxiv-2210-14711.creator: Shoichi KOYAMA and Kazuyuki ARIKAWA (1)
arxiv-2210-14711.description: Abstract ABSTRACT A sound field reproduction method called weighted pressure matching is proposed. Sound field reproduction is aimed at synthesizing the desired sound field using multiple loudspeakers inside a target region. Optimization-based methods are derived from the minimization of errors between synthesized and desired sound fields, which enable the use of an arbitrary array geometry in contrast with integral-equation-based methods.

arxiv-2211-11146.title: Magnetocaloric effect at the reorientation of the magnetization in ferromagnetic multilayers with perpendicular anisotropy
arxiv-2211-11146.creator: Vittorio Basso, Carlo P. Sasso, Martino LoBue, Karl G. Sandeman
arxiv-2211-11146.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Vittorio Basso, Carlo P. Sasso, Martino LoBue, Karl G. Sandeman. We investigate the magnetocaloric effect obtained by the rotation of a magnetic field applied to an exchange-coupled multilayer system composed of two different ferromagnetic (FM) materials. We specifically consider a system in which the two FMs have perpendicular uniaxial anisotropy axes and utilise conditions which yield a reorientation of the total magnetization when compensation between the anisotropies of the two layers occurs. We calculate the consequent entropy change associated with the “artificial" reorientation.

arxiv-2403-02152.title: Non equivalence of Carroll limits in relativistic string theory
arxiv-2403-02152.creator: Roberto Casalbuoni, Daniele Dominici, Joaquim Gomis
arxiv-2403-02152.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Roberto Casalbuoni, Daniele Dominici, Joaquim Gomis. We construct new Carroll strings in flat space by considering the Carroll limit of equivalent relativistic string theories at classical level. In the limit these Carroll strings are no longer equivalent and have different degrees of freedom. This fact is due to a general phenomenon that the configuration space and canonical Lagrangians are no longer equivalent after a singular redefinition of the variables and of the parameters of the starting Lagrangians.

arxiv-2406-11001.title: Symmetries and Interactions of 𝒩 = 1 \mathcal{N}=1 SUGRA: from Constructive and BCFW to KLT formulations
arxiv-2406-11001.description: Abstract In this paper, we study the couplings of the gravity supermultiplet (graviton and gravitino) of minimal 𝒩 = 1 \mathcal{N}=1 SUGRA following a constructive approach. Firstly, we use the master formula that follows from considering the scaling behavior of the spinor variables under the little group. Secondly, we derive the 4-point couplings using BFCW.

arxiv-2506-08165.title: Compact Temporal Geometry and the T 2 T^{2} Framework for Quantum Gravity
arxiv-2506-08165.creator: James C. Hateley
arxiv-2506-08165.description: Abstract We introduce a two-dimensional temporal framework in which time is represented by a compact manifold T 2 = ( t 1 , t 2 ) T^{2}=(t_{1},t_{2}) , with t 1 t_{1} encoding classical causal structure and t 2 t_{2} representing quantum coherence.

arxiv-2509-15487.title: DiskMINT: Self-Consistent Thermochemical Disk Models with Radially Varying Gas and Dust – Application to the Massive, CO-Rich Disk of IM Lup
arxiv-2509-15487.creator: Dingshan Deng, Uma Gorti, Ilaria Pascucci, Maxime Ruaud
arxiv-2509-15487.description: Abstract Disks around young stars are the birthplaces of planets, and the spatial distribution of their gas and dust masses is critical for understanding where and what types of planets can form. We present self-consistent thermochemical disk models built with DiskMINT , which extends its initial framework to allow for spatially decoupled gas and dust distributions.

pmc-10497153.title: Best practice guidelines for professional nurses to provide self-management support to adults with tuberculosis-human immunodeficiency virus coinfection: A scoping review
pmc-10497153.creator: Eric Tornu, Portia Jordan, Michael McCaul
pmc-10497153.description: BackgroundAdults with tuberculosis-human immunodeficiency virus coinfection require professional nurses’ support to manage their illness, treatment and its effect on their daily lives. This scoping review maps recommendations in clinical or best practice guidelines that guide professional nurses to provide self-management support to adults with tuberculosis-human immunodeficiency virus coinfection in primary healthcare settings.

pmc-11389381.title: Putting patients first: when home-based care staff prioritise loyalty to patients above the system and themselves. An ethnographic study
pmc-11389381.creator: Cecilie Knagenhjelm Hertzberg, Morten Magelssen, Anne Kari Tolo Heggestad
pmc-11389381.description: BackgroundThe growing number of older people worldwide poses challenges for health policy, particularly in the Global North, where policymakers increasingly expect seniors to live and receive care at home. However, healthcare professionals, particularly in home-based care, face dilemmas between adhering to care ideals and meeting external demands.

pmc-11487481.title: Mechanical circulatory support as bridge to recovery in an 8-year-old girl with tachycardia-induced cardiomyopathy due to atypical atrioventricular nodal re-entrant tachycardia: a case report
pmc-11487481.creator: Béatrice Susanne Kahl, Manfred Marx, Matthias Gass, Dominik Wiedemann, Ina Michel-Behnke
pmc-11487481.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundIncessant tachycardias can severely impair cardiac function, which is known as tachycardia-induced cardiomyopathy (TIC). The cornerstone of successful therapy is heart rate control. Otherwise, heart failure requiring mechanical circulatory support (MCS) and ultimately heart transplantation may evolve.

pmc-11605005.title: NFE2L2 and SLC25A39 drive cuproptosis resistance through GSH metabolism
pmc-11605005.creator: Jiao Liu, Hu Tang, Fangquan Chen, Changfeng Li, Yangchun Xie, Rui Kang, Daolin Tang
pmc-11605005.description: Cuproptosis is a recently discovered form of regulated cell death triggered by mitochondrial copper accumulation and proteotoxic stress. Here, we provide the first evidence that glutathione (GSH), a major non-protein thiol in cells, acts as a cuproptosis inhibitor in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) cells.

pmc-12446236.title: Effect of Pinus koraiensis leaf extract on fatigue reduction and exercise performance: study protocol for a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial
pmc-12446236.creator: Yujin Choi, Changsop Yang, Ji Soo Yoon, Sunhoo Kim, Sang-Yoon Kim, Mi Young Lee
pmc-12446236.description: BackgroundPrevious research has shown that Pinus koraiensis leaf (PKL) extract exhibits promising anti-fatigue potential in mice, showing improved exercise endurance, decreased stress-related biochemical markers, and enhanced antioxidant activity. Based on this previous animal study, the present study aims to evaluate the efficacy of PKL extract on fatigue reduction and exercise performance in healthy adults with moderate to severe fatigue.

pmc-12574704.title: A comparison of multiple amyloid PET radiotracers for Down syndrome clinical trials
pmc-12574704.creator: Matthew Zammit, Julie Price, Bradley Christian, Michael Rafii, Beau M Ances, Beau M Ances, Howard F Andrews, Karen Bell, Rasmus M Birn, Adam M Brickman, Peter Bulova, Jeff Burns, Amrita Cheema, Kewei Chen, Bradley T Christian, Isabel Clare, Ann D Cohen, Eric W Doran, Tatiana M Foroud, Benjamin L Han
pmc-12574704.description: Adults with Down syndrome carry high risk of developing Alzheimer’s disease and efforts to include this population in clinical trials remain limited. A barrier to recruitment for anti-amyloid trials includes the availability of the same amyloid PET radiotracer to multiple treatment centres.

pmc-12801457.title: HPV genotype distribution and cervical lesion severity in HPV-positive women: a study from the Guizhou Province cervical cancer screening program
pmc-12801457.creator: Xingjing Luo, Ying Chen, Lei He, Sihan Liu, Fei Zhang, Bing Liu, Honghong Zhang, Fan Qi
pmc-12801457.description: ObjectiveTo analyze the infection status and subtype distribution of high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) and their relationship with cervical lesions among women undergoing cervical cancer screening in Guizhou Province, thereby informing HPV vaccine selection and optimizing cervical cancer screening strategies.MethodsData were sourced from the 2024 Guizhou Province free cervical cancer screening program for women.

pmc-12963582.title: Nintedanib enhances the antitumor efficacy of pd-1 blockade, potentially through inhibition of myeloid-derived suppressor cells and cancer-associated fibroblasts
pmc-12963582.creator: Ryo Suzuki, Satoshi Watanabe, Kunihiro Shono, Takaaki Masuda, Kensuke Yanai, Ryo Yamazaki, Yumi Ando, Tomoya Wakabayashi, Susumu Tanaka, Tomoki Sekiya, Kohei Kushiro, Naohiro Yanagimura, Miyuki Sato, Tomohiro Tanaka, Koichiro Nozaki, Yu Saida, Satoshi Hokari, Masashi Arita, Riuko Ohashi, Kenjiro Shi
pmc-12963582.description: Although programmed cell death-1 (PD-1) inhibitors have shown promising and durable responses in patients with several types of cancer, many patients show resistance to PD-1 inhibitors. Recent evidence has demonstrated that immunosuppressive cells are induced in tumor microenvironment and inhibit the anti-tumor effects of anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody (αPD-1 mAb).

pmc-13277626.title: Blurring evidence with advocacy: a systematic review of policy recommendations for net zero
pmc-13277626.creator: Evangelos Danopoulos, Aarushi Shah, Claudia R Schneider, John A D Aston
pmc-13277626.description: Policy recommendations (PRs) now play a crucial role in tackling the climate crisis, underscoring the need for evidence-based, objective and transparent communication. Scientific studies often put forward PRs, but their quality has not yet been evaluated. Here, we systematically appraised the quality of PRs in areas of green energy and transportation for tackling climate change.

pmc-13382614.title: Artificial Intelligence in higher education: use and appropriation of tools by university students
pmc-13382614.creator: Raúl González, Roberto Valdés, Esteban Pérez, Ernesto Leon-Castro
pmc-13382614.description: IntroductionThis research presents the results of the study to analyze the perception of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and its relationship with the learning and Academic Performance of students at a university in northwestern Mexico during the period February to May 2025.MethodAn analytical, cross-sectional study was conducted.

pmc-13447843.title: An uncertainty-aware evaluation framework based on hierarchical vision transformers for robust cross-domain plant leaf disease classification
pmc-13447843.creator: Tripti Shrivastava, Ayush Kumar Agrawal, Abhinav Shukla, Parul Dubey
pmc-13447843.description: Plant leaf disease detection is a critical task in precision agriculture, where reliable diagnosis under real-world conditions is essential for reducing crop losses and supporting timely intervention. Although deep learning models have achieved high classification accuracy, their performance often degrades under domain shift between controlled laboratory datasets and real-field environments, while predictive uncertainty and confidence calibration remain largely unaddressed.

pmc-13538161.title: Cartilage disruption patterns associated with percutaneous intramedullary screw fixation for metatarsal fractures: a cadaveric study
pmc-13538161.creator: Bailey Keith, Joseph Burke, Kelly Hynes, James Baker, Jeannie Huh
pmc-13538161.description: PurposeIntramedullary screw fixation is an emerging technique for operative metatarsal fractures, yet the extent and location of articular cartilage disruption from retrograde screw insertion remain undefined. This study quantifies cartilage surface disruption and maps injury locations in the metatarsal head following screw placement.MethodsFourteen fresh-frozen cadaveric feet (56 lesser metatarsals) underwent standardized retrograde intramedullary screw fixation using 3.6 mm screws.
